component.name: InDuckGo
component.summary: Privacy-first browser with DuckDuckGo's tracker protections

description.p: InDuckGo is a web browser on QtWebEngine (Chromium) that blocks third-party trackers with DuckDuckGo's open-source protections and its own filter lists, upgrades connections to HTTPS and removes tracking parameters from links. It has no extension support, by design.
Every profile and every site installed as an app runs in its own process with its own cookies and storage, so a link clicked in the browser never reaches the session of your bank or mailbox.
InDuckGo is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Duck Duck Go, Inc.
Fixed: the toolbar icons were invisible on a dark bar under Plasma's Breeze style; they are now drawn in the colour of the bar's text.
A tab can be moved to a window of its own: right-click it and choose "Move to New Window", or drag it off the tab strip. The page keeps running.
Cookie dialogs are rejected at once with DuckDuckGo's autoconsent library, Facebook's included, and never accepted. A site whose shield you switched off is left alone.
Fixed: the page scripts were not applied, so DuckDuckGo offered a browser extension the browser does not install and Guard hid no page elements.
InDuckGo now runs on QtWebEngine (Chromium) with a Qt Quick interface, replacing WebKitGTK.

Tracker protection: DuckDuckGo's rules are evaluated as DuckDuckGo evaluates them, advertising and analytics trackers are blocked on every page, connections a page opens before any request are refused, and the protection data is downloaded on first start and kept current. On 12 popular sites 5 trackers got through, against 6 for the WebKitGTK edition, 8 for Brave and 109 for Chrome.
Not yet in this edition: fingerprint and Global Privacy Control protection, the Tor window, automatic rejection of cookie pop-ups, bookmarks and history.
The WebKitGTK browser behaves as in 1.2.0. The shared core gained tab placement, window button style and profile tile preferences for the upcoming Qt edition, which is not packaged yet.
Interface texts for the new features were added to all translations.
The WebKitGTK browser behaves as in 1.1.2. The shared core gained the groundwork of the upcoming Qt edition, which is not packaged yet.
Interface texts for the new features were added to all translations.
Smooth mouse-wheel scrolling: every wheel step is animated like in Chromium, with a switch in the preferences.
Faster scrolling on pages with scroll animations.
Interface language: choose among 68 languages in the preferences.
Downloads: a list in the toolbar, a choice of save folder, a clear-list button and a manager with the whole history.
Faster pages: drawing with GTK's OpenGL renderer instead of copying every frame through memory.
Tor window: browsing through InDuckGo's own Tor, with bridges, onion services and New Identity.
Toolbar: an onion button for the Tor window, and preferences to choose the toolbar's buttons.
New application icon.
